questions.q: In the procure-to-pay chain, which document typically comes immediately BEFORE the supplier invoice?
options: The receipt (or purchase order, if there is no receiving step)
questions.explain: The chain runs requisition, purchase order, receipt, then invoice. The invoice is what Payables compares against the PO and/or receipt.

questions.q: Which statement best describes Payables' relationship to Procurement and Receiving?
options: Payables creates purchase orders and then approves its own receipts
Payables is a downstream consumer of documents that Procurement and Receiving already created
Payables and Procurement are the same module with different names
Receiving happens after Payables pays the invoice
questions.explain: Payables reacts to purchase orders and receipts created upstream; it does not originate them.

questions.q: A Payables user sees a 'quantity billed exceeds quantity received' problem on an invoice. What is the MOST likely underlying cause?
options: The General Ledger period is closed
The supplier's bank account is invalid
Receiving has not yet recorded the delivery of the goods
questions.explain: Quantity-related matching problems are usually caused by an upstream receiving record that doesn't yet reflect what was actually delivered.

questions.q: Which type of invoice does NOT get compared against a purchase order at all?
options: A non-PO invoice coded directly to an account
questions.explain: Non-PO invoices, like a one-off consulting fee or a utility bill, are coded directly to an account with no matching step.

questions.q: Which module in the chain is responsible for actually disbursing funds once an invoice is ready to pay?
questions.explain: Payables prepares the invoice to be paid, but the Payments module owns bank accounts, payment methods, and disbursement.
